Article Title: 'Gukesh's lifetime dream just came too early': American GM Levon Aronian assesses Sindarov clash | Exclusive
Article Text:
Levon Aronian on Javokhir Sindarov vs D Gukesh clash

Mikhail Tal (Photo from Dutch National Archive)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov is not thinking about the summit clash against Dommaraju Gukesh yet.Earlier this year, the 20-year-old Uzbek earned his shot at the title by winning the Cyprus Candidates with a round to spare. But having returned to the country where it all began — it was in India that Sindarov won the FIDE World Cup in Goa in 2025 to qualify for the Candidates — he is keen to talk about everything except the upcoming Geneva encounter, where he will take on Gukesh in a series of 14 classical games running from November 22 to December 13."Right now, I'm focusing on my next events: the Global Chess League and the Olympiad," he told reporters on Friday. "After those, I will start preparing for the World Championship match."The Global Chess League (GCL) begins on Saturday. The Uzbek Grandmaster plays for the American Gambits there, then turns out for his national team at the Olympiad in Samarkand from 15 to 27 September.Gukesh will also represent India at the Chess Olympiad, but the GCL is one of several tournaments he has chosen to skip as he sharpens his focus on the World Championship match.American Grandmaster Levon Aronian senses that the title fight between two 20-year-olds will hinge as much on temperament as on preparation."Gukesh is a big fighter," he told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interview. "He has been a bit down, but I expect him to be in a fighting mood for the match. Of course, it's a tremendous pressure."Gukesh became world champion at 18, the youngest to do so. Aronian sees an echo of an earlier era in that. Mikhail Tal, who won the title at 23 in 1960, was himself the youngest world champion of his time, before Garry Kasparov broke the record 25 years later."You know, you're so young and your lifetime dream just came too early. I think the same kind of thing happened to Mikhail Tal. He also became a world champion too early. And of course, it's normal to be overwhelmed," Aronian added.From a strategic point of view, Aronian feels the wider chess world to have already made up its mind about how Gukesh will approach the match."I think people at the moment, they think that Gukesh is going to go and try to be very cautious, like in the similar style, like Ding (Liren) was doing against Nepomniachtchi, or also the way Ding was playing against Gukesh as well," he said with a smile.Whether that script holds against Sindarov, he added, is the interesting question."There are so many choices to make, and it's definitely going to be an interesting match from a strategical point. I expect Sindarov to be continuing playing very interesting chess the way he's doing. It's an interesting clash, I think. Hopefully, there will be lots of resulting games," he opined.Asked whether failing to win the World Championship title himself was a source of regret, Aronian, who has been ranked World No. 2 and has won world titles in every format except classical, concluded, "I have no regrets whatsoever, because I never valued myself so highly as a chess player. Of course, I have talent, and I'm better than many of the world champions in my understanding of chess. But the way I got to be number two is already a miracle for me; my knowledge of chess was so much worse before.ALSO READ: 'I'm Surprised': Levon Aronian on weakness Praggnanandhaa fixed to win India's historic GCT title | Exclusive "I'm not sure that setting up goals is a good thing for you. Sometimes it just adds to the anxiety. I think it's better just to enjoy and cherish what you have."
Article Summary: World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov is not thinking about the summit clash against Dommaraju Gukesh yet. American Grandmaster Levon Aronian senses that the title fight between two 20-year-olds will hinge as much on temperament as on preparation. Aronian sees an echo of an earlier era in that. Mikhail Tal was himself the youngest world champion of his time.

Article Title: No special ‘room’ for cricket: IOA draws line on BCCI’s Asian Games stay
Article Text:
Indian cricket team (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: If the BCCI decides its cricketers need to stay outside the official Asian Games hotels in Aichi-Nagoya, the board will have to take full responsibility for accommodation, food, transport and ensuring that its players reach the venue on time. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA), meanwhile, will not seek separate accommodation arrangements for cricket, as it’s for the cricket body and Organising Committee (OC) to work out an amicable solution.IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer, speaking to TOI, said the BCCI is free to make its own arrangements if the organisers’ hotels don’t suit its requirements, but the decision and the accompanying logistical responsibility would rest with the Board. The IOA, he stressed, has to ensure equal treatment and the welfare of the entire Indian contingent across 36 sports.“BCCI CEO Hemang Amin got in touch with us (IOA), and we had a fruitful discussion. They are contemplating sending an advance team to Japan to assess the facilities. The IOA is completely fine with that. Based on their assessment, they can decide whether they want to use the organisers’ facilities or make their own arrangements.It is for the BCCI and the organisers to work out the best solution. All sports, athletes, coaches and the entire delegation are treated equally by IOA,” Iyer said.For now, the Games organisers have a designated accommodation plan for both Indian teams. The men have been allotted the three-star APA Hotel Nagoya Ekimae, while the women have been assigned the four-star Meitetsu Grand Hotel, it’s been learnt. Both properties possess the requisite amenities, though they are a grade below the five-star accommodation to which India’s cricketers are generally accustomed. Rooms will be on a twin-sharing basis, another major bone of contention.The women, captained by Harmanpreet Kaur, face the first logistical test. They return from the Asia Cup in Dubai on Sept 13 and are scheduled to fly to Nagoya the following day. Their Asian Games campaign begins directly in the quarterfinals on Sept 18, with their tournament scheduled to conclude on Sept 22.The men, led by Shreyas Iyer , will travel later, leaving for Japan on Sept 21. They too enter directly at the quarterfinal stage, with their campaign running from Sept 28 and the team scheduled to return on Oct 4.With both teams having different arrival windows, the BCCI is now looking at the accommodation and logistics from its own perspective. An advance team is travelling to Japan early next week to inspect the hotels, cricket venue and other facilities before the Board takes a final call, sources revealed.The availability of suitable alternatives could be crucial. Aichi-Nagoya is already under considerable accommodation pressure, with the number of athletes and coaches expected to rise to around 17,000 from an original planning figure of 15,000. Existing hotels are being supplemented by mobile accommodation and the Costa Serena cruise ship.If the BCCI decides the official hotels do not work for its teams and opts for separate properties, it will have to arrange the entire operation, including rooms, food, local transport and travel to and from the cricket venue, while ensuring the players reach the ground well ahead of match time.That arrangement, however, would not put the cricketers outside the Games system. The BCCI would have to communicate its decision through the IOA to the organisers, and all Games-related security, accreditation and access protocols would continue to apply. Outsiders without valid accreditation would not be permitted into the team hotels.The separate stay would also have implications for anti-doping procedures. WADA and International Testing Agency (ITA) dope-control officers would have to be informed of the players’ location so that random testing can be carried out at their chosen accommodation.Iyer said the IOA was comfortable with the BCCI assessing what works best for its players.“The BCCI is taking care of its athletes, and sending an advance team is the right way to assess the facilities before making a decision. We are completely for the well-being of the athletes. Our objective is that the entire Indian delegation has a comfortable stay and a wonderful experience in Japan,” he said.The contrast with Los Angeles 2028 is already emergingWhile Japan’s cricket arrangements have prompted scrutiny, planning for cricket’s Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028 is already well advanced. Iyer was part of a joint IOA-Sports Authority of India (SAI) delegation that recently spent nearly a week in Los Angeles, meeting stakeholders and inspecting facilities across sports, including cricket.“The objective is to ensure athletes can focus only on their performance and do not face logistical issues. We are thinking well in advance about their welfare, comfort and acclimatisation, and this is something which is happening for the first time,” Iyer said.Cricket’s LA28 venue, the newly built Knight Riders Cricket Ground at the Fairplex complex in Pomona, is located next to the Sheraton Fairplex Suites & Conference Center, where the cricket teams are expected to be accommodated. Major League Cricket matches are also expected to provide an early competitive test of the new venue and playing surface.Before the Asian Games, India and Japan will also share a historic cricketing moment. Their men’s teams meet in a T20I on Sept 22 for the Suzuki Cup, marking 75 years of diplomatic relations and giving India valuable match practice ahead of the Games.
Article Summary: If BCCI decides its cricketers need to stay outside the official Asian Games hotels in Aichi-Nagoya, the board will have to take full responsibility for accommodation, food, transport and ensuring that its players reach the venue on time. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA), meanwhile, will not seek separate accommodation arrangements for cricket, as it’s for the cricket body and Organising Committee to work out an amicable solution.

Article Title: More drama in Pakistan cricket: Mohsin Naqvi's PCB likely to remove chief selector Aaqib Javed in 'clean-up' exercise
Article Text:
Aaqib Javed, Mohsin Naqvi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is likely to remove former Test cricketer and chief selector Aaqib Javed from the national selection committee as part of a wider "clean-up" exercise being carried out within the board, news agency PTI reported.The development comes days after senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha were sent home from England. The decision has raised questions over Pakistan's selection policy and team management.“Aqib is also likely to be told to focus on his role as Director Development at the Lahore High Performance Centre,” a source was quoted as saying by PTI.According to the PTI quoted source, the decision to send back Rizwan, Imam and Salman was part of the PCB's wider plan. He claimed that Rizwan and Imam were dropped not only because of their form but also because of their behaviour in the dressing room.“The rest of the players sent back were done so on the recommendation of interim red-ball head coach Mike Hesson, who wanted to try out some players he had worked with in the white-ball camp,” the source was further quoted as saying by PTI.It added that the PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi was keen on a "clean-up" and that the selection committee could be the next area to see changes.“Aaqib, who is considered the blue-eyed boy of the chairman, is also likely to be told to just focus on his role as Director Development at the Lahore High Performance Centre,” he said.Another member of the selection committee, former Pakistan captain Misbah-ul-Haq, has already offered to step down.The PCB has also issued notices to members of the selection committee and advisory committee, asking them to explain the selection of Imam and Rizwan for the England tour and the criteria used to formulate the selection policy.Aaqib has been one of the influential figures within the PCB and has had a significant role in selection and other team-related matters.Pakistan suffered an innings and 103-run loss in the series opener at Headingley before going down by 194 runs at Lord's on Sunday as England took an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.The Pakistan Cricket Board responded to those defeats in dramatic fashion, taking the extraordinary step of sending seven players home, calling up another seven and replacing sacked Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Hesson, already Pakistan's white-ball boss.Senior players Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, who was Pakistan's captain at Headingley when Babar Azam was injured, were among those told to leave.
Article Summary: Pakistan Cricket Board likely to remove Aaqib Javed from national selection committee as part of a wider "clean-up" exercise. The development comes days after senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha were sent home from England. The decision has raised questions over Pakistan's selection policy and team management.

Article Title: In first appearance since 2022, Serena and Venus Williams lose US Open doubles thriller after 5-0 lead in decider
Article Text:
Serena Williams, left, and Venus Williams play against Hao-Ching Chan, and Maya Joint, during a women's doubles match at the US Open tennis championships, Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Serena and Venus Williams ' return to the US Open women's doubles after four years ended in a three-set defeat to Chan Hao-ching and Maya Joint at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday.The Williams sisters lost 3-6, 7-6 (8-6), 7-6 (10-7) after leading the deciding 10-point tiebreak 5-0.The pair had not played Grand Slam doubles together since the 2022 US Open. For Serena Williams, it was also her first appearance at Flushing Meadows since that tournament.Serena, now 44, returned to professional tennis this year after stepping away from the sport. Venus, 46, has continued playing on the WTA Tour.The match swung several times before the sisters forced a deciding tiebreak. They raced to a 5-0 lead, but both players committed double faults during the tiebreak as Chan and Joint came back to win the final seven points.It was also Serena's second loss to Maya Joint this summer. The Australian had beaten Serena in three sets at Wimbledon during Serena's return to Grand Slam singles. The sisters later pulled out of their Wimbledon doubles match after Serena injured her knee.The atmosphere at Arthur Ashe Stadium was electric. The Williams sisters received a loud ovation as they walked onto the court wearing matching white outfits.The crowd cheered almost every point won by the Americans, and the noise grew even louder when they took control of the deciding tiebreak.After the match, Joint said playing against the sisters was a memorable experience."The atmosphere was surreal. Being able to play aginst such legends of the game is super special."Venus and Serena are among the most successful doubles teams in tennis history. Together, they won 14 Grand Slam women's doubles titles, including two US Open crowns, and Olympic gold medals in 2000, 2008 and 2012. They also held the world No. 1 doubles ranking for eight weeks.
Article Summary: Serena and Venus Williams lose in three sets to Chan Hao-ching and Maya Joint. The pair had not played Grand Slam doubles together since the 2022 US Open. Serena, 44, returned to professional tennis this year after stepping away from the sport.

Article Title: Seven wickets in 21 balls: Sri Lanka's Chamari Athapaththu scripts history with record-breaking spell
Article Text:
Chamari Athapaththu

Defending champions Sri Lanka moved to the top of Group B in the Women's Asia Cup after beating Indonesia by 75 runs in Dubai on Thursday, thanks to captain Chamari Athapaththu's record seven-wicket haul and Nilakshika Silva's half-century.Sri Lanka were defending a modest target of 125 on a slow-paced pitch, but Athapaththu turned the match around with one of the best bowling performances in women's T20 internationals.She came on to bowl in the fourth over and struck with her fourth, seventh and eighth deliveries. Although she missed out on a hat-trick in that over, she completed it later by taking three wickets in three balls across two overs.Athapaththu finished with 7/5 in 21 balls, becoming the first bowler from a Full Member nation to take seven wickets in a women's T20I. The previous best figures in women's T20Is belonged to Zimbabwe's Esther Mbofana, who took 6/11 against Eswatini in 2021.Indonesia were bowled out for 49. Rahmawati Pangestuti scored 10, while Ni Made Putri Suwandewi remained unbeaten on 12. No other Indonesian batter reached double figures.Earlier, Sri Lanka were in trouble at 62/6 before Nilakshika Silva scored 50 off 35 balls to lift them to 124/7.For Indonesia, Ni Luh Dewi was the pick of the bowlers with 3/32.The win took Sri Lanka to the top of Group B in the Women's Asia Cup.In Group A, India remain on top of the standings, with Pakistan in second place.Meanwhile, India's vice-captain Smriti Mandhana also made history during India's Group A match against Hong Kong in Dubai. The 30-year-old went past Mithali Raj to become the highest run-scorer in women's international cricket across all formats.
Article Summary: Sri Lanka beat Indonesia by 75 runs in the Women's Asia Cup in Dubai. Captain Chamari Athapaththu took a record seven-wicket haul. Nilakshika Silva scored 50 off 35 balls to lift Sri Lanka to 124/7.

Article Title: ‘AAF risk’: Herbal supplements put India’s Asian Games athletes under scanner
Article Text:
Herbal Supplemets (Representational Image)

Unprecedented scrutiny

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengaluru: With Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) officials conducting random checks on India’s elite athletes preparing for the Asian Games, experts are concerned that the use of herbal supplements by top athletes could result in Adverse Analytical Findings (AAF) when samples are tested for performance-enhancing substances at WADA-accredited laboratories abroad.According to experts, the use of herbal supplements is quite common among athletes training in national camps.“Among the supplements commonly used by our athletes are kida jadi buti, bhasmas, ashwagandha and shilajit. Kida jadi (Cordyceps sinensis) is the most expensive of the lot, retailing at Rs 16-20 lakh per kilogram. It is consumed after being mixed with honey,” they told TOI.In India, kida jadi is listed on e-commerce platforms at around Rs 1.66 lakh for 100g.“There are many athletes who use their savings to buy kida jadi and consume it regularly. There is a risk of an AAF for athletes using herbal supplements, as many of these products are not tested for their ingredients. For a month’s course, they may have to shell out around Rs 1 lakh.“A lot of our sprinters, throwers and middle-distance runners are taking these supplements,” they said, adding that most athletes do not disclose their use of herbal supplements when declaring the list of supplements they consume.Kida jadi is a type of fungus sourced from the Himalayas. Indian athletes have been using it for many years and none have returned a positive result so far. However, there have recently been concerns that some products may contain substances on WADA’s banned list, though nothing has been confirmed yet.“These metabolites may not have triggered a positive result in NADA tests, but in advanced tests conducted by the AIU, the outcome could be different, putting our athletes at risk of an AAF,” experts said.Asked about the use of locally sourced herbal supplements, Mihira Khopkar, who served as the Indian contingent’s nutritionist at the Paris Olympics, confirmed the risks involved.“In elite sport, it is almost non-negotiable that high-performing athletes choose supplements that are not only evidence-based but also third-party tested,” she told TOI.Athletics coaches, both former and current, who have followed India’s progress over the past few decades, recalled that Indian athletes have never undergone such intense testing before a major Games.“What the AIU has done on behalf of WADA is targeted testing of India’s top athletes who will be competing at the Asian Games. Across Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar and Patiala, officials have tested most athletes in the squad. This is the first time they have conducted such large-scale random testing of Indian athletes ahead of a major meet,” sources told TOI.“A few years ago, WADA attempted to test Indian athletes training in Potchefstroom, South Africa, but achieved limited success as many were unavailable. Athletes cannot be penalised for missing random tests, unlike those in the Registered Testing Pool (RTP), who are bound by the whereabouts clause,” they added.After testing athletes residing at the Kalinga Stadium complex in Bhubaneswar, officials also conducted checks on those training in Bengaluru at the Anju Bobby Sports Foundation and the SAI South Centre.India topped the AIU’s list of doping offenders in July this year with 162 names, ahead of Kenya (148) and Russia (60). The AIU also reclassified the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) from Category B to Category A.“Unfortunately, the quality of the domestic anti-doping programme is simply not proportionate to the doping risk,” AIU Chair David Howman had said.
Article Summary: The Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) is conducting random checks on India’s elite athletes preparing for the Asian Games. Experts are concerned that the use of herbal supplements could result in Adverse Analytical Findings (AAF) when samples are tested for performance-enhancing substances abroad.

Article Title: 'A bit abnormal': After shock second-round exit at US Open, Auger-Aliassime reveals he 'was seeing spots'
Article Text:
Felix Auger-Aliassime, of Canada, serves the ball to Karen Khachanov, of Russia, during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Karen Khachanov knocked out third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime from the US Open on Thursday, winning 6-7(5), 6-3, 6-2, 6-2 to reach the third round.The Russian, ranked No. 50 in the world, came into the tournament after losing the opening match in all three of his US Open warm-up events. But he took advantage of an off-colour Auger-Aliassime, whose level dropped as the match went on at Louis Armstrong Stadium.After the match, Auger-Aliassime said he started feeling unwell during the contest and struggled to recover."After a set and a half, I just couldn't feel well and was dizzy and seeing spots and couldn't recover," he said, as quoted by BBC. "I thought maybe it would pass, but it didn't."I've never felt quite like that. I've had cramps before. I've felt tired towards the end of matches, but in a normal way."This was abnormal a little bit, and there were no signs in the last couple of days and no signs this morning, as well."The defeat made Auger-Aliassime the highest-ranked player to exit the men's singles draw so far in New York.Khachanov, who reached the US Open semi-finals in 2022, broke the Canadian's serve seven times during the match. He also saved seven of the nine break points he faced.The win is only Khachanov's second victory over a top-10 player at a Grand Slam and sends him into the third round in New York.The result meant Khachanov has now reached the third round of all four Grand Slam tournaments in a single ​calendar year for the first time.
Article Summary: Karen Khachanov knocked out third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime from the US Open. Russian, ranked No. 50 in the world, won 6-7(5), 6-3, 6-2,6-2 to reach the third round.

Article Title: Kidambi Srikanth pulls off stunning upset, Satwik-Chirag reach China Masters quarterfinals
Article Text:
Kidambi Srikanth

Former world No. 1 Kidambi Srikanth produced a stunning comeback to upset world No. 9 Victor Lai of Canada, while the men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty battled a mid-match slump to reach the quarterfinals of the China Masters Super 750 badminton tournament in Shenzhen on Thursday.There was disappointment, however, for young Tanvi Sharma and the mixed doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto.Tanvi fought hard against Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki but went down 17-21, 21-18, 16-21.Dhruv and Tanisha suffered an 18-21, 18-21 defeat to Liu Kuang Heng and Hsu Yin Hui of Chinese Taipei.Srikanth, the 2021 World Championships silver medallist, displayed remarkable fighting spirit to overcome World Championships bronze medallist Lai 21-18, 21-19.Later, he said: “I was only thinking about what I have been doing throughout the match and what I need to do going forward.”Srikanth added: “He has been playing well for the last 12-14 months. But I felt I’ll have my chances if I can play my best. I wasn’t thinking about how he has been playing. I was only thinking about how I should play.”Srikanth will next take on Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu for a place in the semifinals.Meanwhile, Satwiksairaj and Chirag overcame a determined challenge from Frenchmen Christo Popov and Toma Junior Popov to register a 21-15, 22-24, 21-9 victory.They now face the Danish pair of Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen in the quarterfinals.

Article Title: Treesa-Gayatri’s coach missing from list, WFI finally clears foreign coaches
Article Text:
India's Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Pullela (ANI Photo)

New Delhi:

WFI finally relents on foreign coaches

Only seven grooms in equestrian

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In squash, Willstrop will be foreign coach

Hockey without women’s masseuse

India’s latest women’s doubles hope, BWF World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, will head to the Asian Games without their dedicated coach B Sumeeth Reddy, whose name does not figure in the official coaching and support staff list for badminton, while the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) has finally agreed to send all three foreign coaches despite its initial reluctance, following a Sports Authority of India (SAI) rebuke.Reddy, a former Olympian who retired in March 2025, has specifically worked with Treesa and Gayatri since then, while also overseeing other women’s doubles players at the Pullela Gopichand Academy in Hyderabad. He was a constant presence in their coaching corner at international events and during the recent Worlds in New Delhi, sitting alongside Gopichand and guiding the pair through their matches.Treesa and Gayatri ended India’s 15-year wait for a women’s doubles medal at the Worlds since 2011, producing a string of impressive performances to claim bronze.Their Asian Games place had earlier come under scrutiny after sports authorities questioned their selection against the prescribed criteria, with Priya Konjengbam and Shruti Mishra emerging as alternatives. Badminton Association of India (BAI) defended the selection on rankings and recent performances.TOI contacted a senior federation official to ascertain whether Reddy’s name had originally been forwarded to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) as an official women’s doubles coach.A call to a BAI official did not elicit a response.It has been learnt that Gopichand will carry the primary responsibility of guiding Treesa and Gayatri in Reddy’s absence. Tan Kim Her, who specifically works with Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, could assist the women’s pair if schedules do not clash. South Korean Yong Sung Yoo, Lakshya Sen’s personal coach has received clearance. Twelve coaching and support personnel have been named for the 20-member badminton team.For wrestling’s 16-member squad, 14 coaching and support personnel have been listed, with all three foreign coaches now set to travel: Georgia’s Emzarios Bentinidis (men’s freestyle), Russia’s Gogi Koguashvili (greco-roman) and Japan’s Kosei Akaishi (women’s team). WFI had initially resisted sending them, preferring Indian coaches over them, but agreed after SAI questioned their omission.According to sources, the Equestrian Federation of India’s (EFI) ad-hoc committee had proposed 20 grooms for the eight-member equestrian team, but only seven have received clearance. The 12-member coaching and support staff list includes Nico Wienstroer, Katharina Asbeck, Kyra Anne Jonkers, Jill Van Osselt, Tabea Linhardt, Johanna Aini Katariina Pohjonen and Alyson Renee Roy as the seven grooms.SAI had also sought an explanation over the original proposal, with no groom named for dressage rider Jai Sud or eventing specialist Arjan Nagra.Former world No. 1 James Willstrop has been granted the SAI’s clearance to serve as India’s foreign squash coach receiving the nod for the same. The Englishman is expected to arrive in Chennai on Sept 17 before travelling with the team.The 40-member hockey squad has 14 support staff, and male masseur Arup Naskar is the sole masseur listed.
Article Summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will head to the Asian Games without their dedicated coach B Sumeeth Reddy. The Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) has finally agreed to send all three foreign coaches despite its initial reluctance. Former world No. 1 James Willstrop has been granted the SAI's clearance to serve as India’s foreign squash coach receiving the nod for the same.

Glasgow Commonwealth Games bronze medallist javelin thrower Yashvir Singh has been drafted into India’s Asian Games athletics squad, replacing two-time Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra , who was ruled out for the season following an ankle ligament tear.Yashvir, who recently threw a personal best of 85.41m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, will team up with the in-form Rohit Yadav (personal best 87.05m) to anchor India’s two-member men’s javelin campaign at Aichi-Nagoya.Meanwhile, former long jumper and Athletics Federation of India (AFI) senior vice-president Anju Bobby George will not travel as team leader, it’s been learnt. Though proposed by the AFI, her name was not cleared by the sports ministry adhering to its guidelines which say: IOA will ensure that any person, if he/she is holding elected position in EC of IOA, any NSF or any sports body, whose name has been included in the list of team officials, will be treated at no cost to the govt.The final athletics squad strength has been pruned to 77. Distance runner Abhishek Pal was dropped after testing positive for clomiphene. “It is not a case of returning dope positive, but as National Anti Doping Agency (NADA) investigates, we don’t want to take any risks,” said AFI planning committee chairman Lalit Bhanot. Additionally, 110m hurdler Tejas Shirse was ruled out due to foot stress fractures suffered during CWG.These two exclusions offset the latest addition of six athletes — Harita Bhadra (200m), Kiran Pahal (400m), Sindhushree G (pole vault), I Asha Ilango (triple jump), Sanya Yadav (discus), and Praveen Kumar (hammer throw) — who were cleared by the ministry after the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) accepted IOA’s late request for their addition, bringing the count from 73 to 79 before Pal and Shirse’s omissions brought the contingent size down to 77.AFI is also seeking approval for Hangzhou double-medallist Avinash Sable to compete in the 5,000m alongside his confirmed 3,000m steeplechase event. However, Sable must first breach the AFI qualification mark of 13:39.18s at the Indian Athletics Series Finals here on Sept 10, where most Asian Games-bound athletes will compete.-- Born in Devsar, Haryana and raised in Jaipur, Raj.-- Shifted from basketball to javelin at age 13, initially practicing with bamboo javelins.-- Coached by his father Rai Singh, a former Indian Railways national champion.-- Broke Chopra’s U-20 Federation Cup record in 2021; joined the 80m club in 2022 (82.13m).-- Overcame major shoulder surgery in late 2023 that kept him out for nearly a year.-- Claimed bronze at Glasgow CWG with a final-throw personal best of 85.41m.-- Became only the third Indian male javelin medallist in CWG history after Kashinath Naik and Chopra.

Article Title: 'Encroacher' remark hangs over Yusuf Pathan as former India cricketer turned politician withdraws Gujarat high court appeal over Vadodara land dispute: Case explained
Article Text:
Yusuf Pathan (ANI Photo)

Pathan had challenged land allotment rejection

VMC had asked Pathan to vacate plot

The Gujarat High Court on Monday dismissed as withdrawn an appeal filed by former India cricketer and Lok Sabha MP Yusuf Pathan against a single-judge order that had described him as an “encroacher” on a piece of government land in Vadodara.Pathan’s lawyer, Shalin Mehta, sought permission to withdraw the plea before a division bench comprising Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal and Justice DN Ray. The lawyer told the court that Pathan’s claim over the land was still being pursued under a state government policy.The division bench subsequently dismissed the appeal as withdrawn.The 43-year-old had approached the High Court challenging a single-judge order that upheld the Gujarat government’s decision to reject his request for allotment of the 978-square metre plot owned by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC).Pathan had claimed the land under a state policy applicable to international cricketers.During an earlier hearing, Pathan had told the court that he was pursuing his claim under a state government scheme and was given four weeks to pursue the matter. The High Court had also warned that he could face higher payment of damages if he took longer to vacate the plot.During Monday’s proceedings, Mehta said they were awaiting a response from the VMC but had not received one.“Because we are saying that there is a circular which allows international cricketers to be given a plot. I think I will withdraw because I haven’t heard anything from them (VMC). I have taken instructions from my client…if it is to happen, it will happen outside the court; otherwise it won’t happen," Mehta submitted.With the appeal withdrawn, Pathan’s attempt to challenge the earlier court order through the division bench has come to an end.The dispute dates back to 2024, when the Gujarat government rejected Pathan’s request for allotment of the plot. Despite the rejection, he continued to occupy the land.After Pathan was elected from the Baharampur Lok Sabha seat in West Bengal on a Trinamool Congress (TMC) ticket in 2024, the VMC issued him a notice asking him to vacate the land. Pathan refused and challenged the matter in court.The High Court had previously taken a strong view of his occupation of the plot. During a hearing on June 8, the court came down heavily on Pathan over the alleged “encroachment” and orally questioned how he could enter and occupy the land without completing the required formalities.The matter now moves outside the court as Pathan continues to pursue his claim under the state policy.
Article Summary: Gujarat High Court dismisses appeal filed by former India cricketer Yusuf Pathan. Pathan had challenged a single-judge order that had described him as an “encroacher’ on a piece of government land in Vadodara. The 43-year-old had approached the High Court challenging the decision.

Article Title: The long game: Inside MLB's big bet on India's baseball future
Article Text:

A future where his job disappears

NEW DELHI: When Major League Baseball (MLB) opened its office in India in 2019, it wasn't the beginning of its journey in India. It was the culmination of a 15-year wait.For Ryo Takahashi, MLB's Director of International Business and the man leading its operations in India, the timing wasn't driven by a grand strategic moment or a blockbuster announcement. It was simply when years of conversations finally turned into an official commitment."People think MLB suddenly discovered India in 2019," Takahashi said in a free-wheeling chat with TimesofIndia.com. "The reality is we had been discussing India for almost 15 years before opening the office. There wasn't a magical reason why it happened in 2019. That's simply when we received the approvals and could make the commitment official," he said.Seven years later, MLB's ambitions in India still look very different from those of most global sports leagues. There are no plans for a professional franchise, no immediate push for a domestic league and no obsession with television ratings. Instead, the league is betting on a deceptively simple idea: if enough children pick up a baseball, everything else will eventually follow.India became MLB's sixth international office after Japan, Mexico, China, the UK and the Dominican Republic.But unlike those markets, baseball arrived with almost no cultural footprint here. That forced the league to begin by listening rather than selling."We don't believe we have all the answers," Takahashi says. "The NBA, La Liga, the Premier League -- they've all spent years understanding Indian fans. I have friends and colleagues across those organisations, and we've learnt as much from their mistakes as their successes," he added.Rather than copying another league's blueprint, MLB chose to build its own Indian version: one centred on schools, grassroots coaching and local storytelling. Since 2019, it has introduced the First Pitch programme in schools across Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, launched the MLB Cup youth tournament and produced India-focused documentaries to make baseball feel more relatable.Ask Takahashi when India will produce its first Major League player, and he gently rejects the premise."People ask us when India will produce an MLB player. That's the wrong starting point," he says. "If one out of every hundred children who tries baseball decides to keep playing, that's already a victory. In a country of India's size, one per cent becomes a very big number."For MLB, participation is the primary currency, not finding elite talent."Our responsibility is to create opportunities. Whether that child eventually plays for an MLB club or simply falls in love with baseball, both outcomes help grow the sport," he reasoned.That thinking explains why MLB measures success through expanding coaching networks, more schools adopting baseball and the remarkable growth of the MLB Cup, which has evolved from just 12 teams in its inaugural edition into a nationwide youth competition involving thousands of participants.Conventional wisdom says cricket makes life impossible for another bat-and-ball sport. Takahashi argues the opposite."Cricket isn't our competitor. It might actually be our biggest advantage," he says. "Indian kids already grow up throwing, catching and hitting a ball. Those athletic foundations are already there," he explained.He has watched six-year-olds experience baseball for the first time and noticed how naturally many adapt."We don't have to teach them how to throw; we just have to show them a different game."MLB's objective isn't replacing cricket but borrowing from its ecosystem. Familiar movements reduce the learning curve, making baseball feel less foreign than many assume.Baseball's biggest obstacle in India isn't awareness alone. It's the clock.Most MLB games unfold in the early hours of the morning for Indian audiences, creating what Takahashi calls a classic chicken-and-egg problem.Even with broadcast partnerships in place with JioStar, he knows the league's target audience isn't awake."We want children to watch baseball, become curious and then play," he says. "But our games often happen at two or three in the morning in India.""An eight-year-old probably isn't holding the TV remote at that time. So maybe today's player becomes tomorrow's viewer. That's the journey we're trying to build."It's why MLB sees broadcasting as supporting grassroots rather than replacing it. A child introduced to baseball in school today may become the adult streaming the World Series a decade later.Perhaps Takahashi's most counterintuitive belief concerns infrastructure. While many emerging sports demand facilities first, MLB believes demand must precede concrete."People often say India needs baseball stadiums first," he says. "We actually think it works the other way around. First you create players, then you create demand, and eventually the infrastructure follows."He points to countless sporting cultures where children develop elite skills using improvised equipment and open spaces."Kids don't need a perfect baseball diamond to learn baseball. Skills come before stadiums."India already has cricket grounds, football fields and school playgrounds. For now, those are enough.That philosophy extends into MLB's biggest fan-facing initiative yet. Scheduled for October 24 in Mumbai, MLBX isn't designed as a traditional baseball tournament. It's a festival. Headed to the Mumbai Football Arena, Andheri Sports Complex, for MLBX are legends of the New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox, two-time defending champions Los Angeles Dodgers and Chicago Cubs."We asked ourselves: cricket evolved from Test matches to T20, football embraced futsal -- what’s baseball's version of that for India? MLBX is our answer," says Takahashi.The format features shorter games, compact fields, home-run contests, music performances and food inspired by classic American ballparks with Indian flavours. Baseball remains the centrepiece, but culture is the hook.The format or the tournament in itself is not new. MLBX is a mixed 3-on-3 baseball competition that combines power hitting, athletic defensive plays and fast-paced gameplay. The competition made its appearance during MLB All-Star Week in Philadelphia. The event has previously taken place at 15 US venues over the past three years, as well as internationally in London, Seoul and Mexico City."It's not just about games," Takahashi says. "It's home-run contests, music, food, culture and entertainment. We want someone to leave Mumbai thinking, 'That was fun... now let me find out more about baseball.'"He says the partnership with former India T20I captain and Mumbai Indians player Suryakumar Yadav has already generated a noticeable spike in enquiries, reinforcing MLB's belief that collaborating with cricket opens doors rather than closes them.Takahashi smiles when asked where he wants baseball in India to be by 2031. "My dream is to do such a good job that I make myself unemployed," he says almost with a grin.The answer is less about personal ambition than institutional success. He imagines an India with thousands more children playing baseball, a genuine national talent pathway, an active Indian national team and perhaps even baseball featuring if India hosts the 2036 Olympics."If, by 2031, baseball has become part of everyday sporting conversations in India, we've done our job," he says.For a league often associated with packed American ballparks and century-old rivalries, MLB's Indian strategy is strikingly patient. Its biggest victory may not be selling out a stadium. It may simply be convincing one child in a school playground to swap a cricket bat for a baseball bat.
Article Summary: Major League Baseball (MLB) opened its office in India in 2019. MLB's ambitions in India still look very different from those of most global sports leagues. There are no plans for a professional franchise, no immediate push for a domestic league. MLB is betting on a deceptively simple idea: if enough children pick up a baseball, everything else will eventually follow.

The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to send seven players and two coaches home after defeats in the first two Tests against England continues to throw up fresh details, with behavioural concerns reportedly playing a role in the removal of senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha.Pakistan suffered defeats in the opening two matches of the series, prompting the PCB to make a sweeping change ahead of the third and final Test in Edgbaston. Test coach Sarfaraz has already been replaced by Mike Hesson, while the white-ball coach will oversee the team for the final Test. Rizwan ’s performances were one of the concerns surrounding the wicketkeeper-batter. He managed just 61 runs across the four innings he played and came under further criticism for his shot selection during the Lord’s Test. His reading of the game also attracted scrutiny.Imam, meanwhile, did not bat in either innings at Lord’s after suffering a calf strain. His decision not to take the field with the bat sparked questions over his commitment, with his injury becoming a major talking point.Agha’s situation was different. He captained Pakistan in the first Test in Babar’s absence but was dropped for the second match before being sent home ahead of the Edgbaston Test.According to news agency PTI, however, the decisions involving Rizwan and Imam were not linked exclusively to their performances. Behavioural issues in the dressing room were also reportedly taken into consideration.The trio of Rizwan, Imam and Agha are now expected to appear before a committee and explain their conduct in connection with certain incidents during Pakistan’s tours of the West Indies and England.The other players sent back from England were reportedly removed from the squad following Hesson’s recommendation. The interim red-ball head coach wanted to assess several white-ball specialists with whom he had previously worked.“The rest of the players sent back were done so on the recommendation of interim red-ball head coach Mike Hesson, who wanted to try out some players he had worked with in the white-ball camp,” a source said.The latest developments are also expected to have consequences for Pakistan’s selection committee. Senior selector Aaqib Javed could be removed as part of a wider clean-up being planned by PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi.Another major development came earlier this week when selector Misbah-ul-Haq tendered his resignation. It remains unclear whether the PCB has formally accepted it.Misbah’s resignation followed the PCB issuing a show-cause notice to the selection committee. The board sought an explanation over the inclusion of Imam and Rizwan in the Test squad for the West Indies and England tours.The PCB has also issued notices to members of its selection and advisory committees, asking them to explain the decision to pick Imam and Rizwan for the England tour and the criteria used to formulate the selection policy.The shake-up could lead to a new selection committee being appointed once the England tour concludes.“A new selection committee could be announced after the England tour,” the source said.Meanwhile, Hesson could remain in charge beyond the England series. The PCB is reportedly keen to appoint him as the permanent head coach, although the move will depend on whether the New Zealander agrees to take up the role.For now, the focus remains on the fallout from the dramatic squad changes. Rizwan, Imam and Salman are expected to face a committee over their alleged behaviour, while Aaqib Javed’s position on the selection panel is also under threat as Naqvi looks to overhaul the PCB’s cricketing structure.
Article Summary: Pakistan Cricket Board sent seven players and two coaches home after defeats in the first two Tests against England. Behavioural concerns reportedly played a role in the removal of senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha. Test coach Sarfaraz has already been replaced by Mike Hesson, while the white-ball coach will oversee the team for the final Test.

Article Title: 'Want him to become a legend’: BCCI reveals plan to nurture Vaibhav Sooryavanshi like Sachin Tendulkar

Mumbai: The BCCI is adopting a cautious route to deal with the rise of 15-year-old batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The board and its key officials are determined to ensure his early success develops into a long and distinguished international career and does not fizzle out after a couple of years of fame and stardom.Following a Team India performance review meeting at the BCCI headquarters on Thursday, board secretary Devajit Saikia said the teenager is being closely monitored, with the board keen to nurture him along the lines of legends such as Sachin Tendulkar “We want Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, or any player of his stature, to continue and serve like Sachin Tendulkar did for the country and become a legend. We are monitoring him from every angle and every step he takes in his international career,” Saikia said.Sooryavanshi has rapidly progressed from IPL sensation to India’s youngest men’s international debutant. He recently became the youngest player to score a Duleep Trophy fifty, hammering 92 off 81 balls, including seven sixes, for East Zone against Central Zone in Bengaluru.Making it clear that the BCCI is focused on longevity rather than instant success, Saikia added: “We are very cautious that every step he takes forward is the right one so that he does not become a one-series or one-year wonder.”Like Tendulkar, Sooryavanshi has burst onto the international scene as a teenager and quickly captured the imagination of Indian cricket fans. The left-hander earned his maiden India call-up after two sensational seasons with Rajasthan Royals .In IPL 2026, he piled up 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.30, scoring a century and five fifties while smashing a record 72 sixes in a single season. After a slow start in England, he bounced back impressively in the T20I series against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches and claiming his first Player of the Series award.Meanwhile, Saikia said the BCCI has no immediate concerns about accommodation or facilities for India’s cricket teams at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.“There is no such issue which we have discussed or which is in our agenda,” he said.However, he made it clear that the board would step in if required.“If any situation arises, we will ensure our players and support staff get the best facilities. If required, the BCCI will have its own system in place to provide them.”

Pakistan's interim Test coach Mike Hesson has denied reports that Salman Ali Agha refused to attend a meeting with King Charles III, saying the story was completely false and describing it as "unacceptable journalism."A report by UK-based The Telegraph on Thursday claimed that one of the players dropped from Pakistan's Test squad had refused to attend a meeting with the UK monarch.Hesson dismissed the report and said Salman had been informed well in advance that he would not be part of the Buckingham Palace visit.Hesson said Salman did not attend the audience with the King because he was part of the trio of players dropped from the squad first and, as a result, Salman, Imam and Rizwan were taken from the list of attendees to Clarence House, BBC reported."Look, I know there's been a void in the news, but people are just making up stories. Article Title: ‘Don’t call it cricket’: Ricky Ponting makes radical T20 pitch to win over US fans
Article Text:
Ricky Ponting (Getty Images)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Australian great Ricky Ponting has suggested a radical change in the way cricket is marketed in the United States, saying administrators should consider dropping the word ‘cricket’ altogether and promoting the sport simply as ‘T20’.With the United States emerging as a key part of the International Cricket Council (ICC)’s global growth strategy, Ponting believes the traditional name could be holding the sport back in a market more familiar with baseball, American football and basketball.The former Australia captain feels the word ‘cricket’ could lead new American audiences to immediately think of Test matches and their five-day format, rather than the shorter and more entertainment-driven T20 game.Speaking to The Athletic, Ponting acknowledged that he is a traditionalist who played far more Test cricket than T20 cricket. However, he said he would be open to a complete rebranding of the format if it helped attract a new generation of American sports fans.“If I was bringing it here wholly and solely to sell and promote the game, I wouldn’t call it cricket," Ponting begins. “It’d just be rebranded as T20 only. Leave the cricket thing aside.As soon as young people hear cricket in parts of the world where they’re not brought up on the game, they think about it being a long, drawn-out, five-day game, and it’s not that."Ponting also believes baseball could provide a useful comparison for introducing T20 to an American audience. Rather than focusing on the technical differences between the sports, he wants potential fans to understand the high-scoring nature of the shortest cricket format.“I would compare it to baseball as much as I could and give kids that chance to understand you’re hitting 15 sixes per game in a game of T20 cricket, but you are hitting less than one home run a game in the game of baseball."The United States has become one of the ICC’s biggest development priorities, given the size and commercial strength of its sports market. While baseball, American football and basketball remain dominant, soccer has also been growing rapidly in the country.Cricket, meanwhile, has traditionally had a much smaller mainstream following in the US and has largely been played and followed by Asian, European and African expat communities.The ICC has been attempting to broaden that audience through a series of major initiatives. The country hosted a successful T20 World Cup in 2024, while Major League Cricket has been developed as a domestic competition. Ponting himself is involved in the league as coach of Washington Freedom.The ICC is also working towards cricket’s return to the Olympic stage at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, with efforts underway to develop suitable grounds and infrastructure in the US.With T20 at the centre of many of those efforts, Ponting believes presenting the sport as a fast-paced, modern product rather than immediately associating it with Test cricket could help the ICC connect with American audiences.
Article Summary: Ricky Ponting has suggested a radical change in the way cricket is marketed in the United States. The former Australia captain feels the word ‘cricket’ could lead new American audiences to immediately think of Test matches and their five- day format. Ponting also believes baseball could provide a useful comparison for introducing T20 to an American audience.

Article Title: ‘Even my wife is watching’: Srikkanth says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is making cricket exciting again

NEW DELHI: Former India opener Kris Srikkanth believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the potential to become one of the biggest names in world cricket, with the teenage sensation already generating an unusual level of excitement around the game.Sooryavanshi, just 15, has continued his rapid rise by making a mark in the Duleep Trophy after already setting the IPL and international stages alight. He's smashing medium pacers with no worries for straight sixes in red-ball cricket. He's toying with the bowlers,” he said.Sooryavanshi's rise has been extraordinary. His breakthrough IPL 2026 campaign with Rajasthan Royals saw him score 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.30, including a century and five fifties. His 72 sixes were an IPL record for a single season, while he collected the Orange Cap, Most Valuable Player, Emerging Player, Super Striker and Super Sixes awards.He subsequently became India's youngest men's international debutant during the T20I series against England. Against Zimbabwe, he scored 151 runs in three matches to help India complete a 3-0 sweep and collected his maiden Player of the Series award.His impact has also extended to age-group cricket. Earlier this year, Sooryavanshi amassed 439 runs at the ICC Under-19 World Cup and was named Player of the Tournament.The BCCI is now taking a cautious, long-term approach to his development. Secretary Devajit Saikia said the board is monitoring the teenager closely and wants his early success to translate into a career similar to those of India's past legends.“We want Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or any player of his stature to continue and serve like Sachin Tendulkar did for the country or other players who in the past became legends,” Saikia said.“So we look at Vaibhav in a very serious manner. He's monitored from every angle and every step he is taking forward in his international career. The BCCI is taking a very close look at his future.”The board's priority, Saikia stressed, is to ensure Sooryavanshi's emergence is not merely a brief burst of teenage brilliance.“You see, the BCCI can be proud that we are promoting a player of the age of 15 years who is already making his mark in the international scenario and we are very cautious that every right step he should take forward so that it should not be a one series or one year wonder,” he said.For now, though, Srikkanth sees something even bigger taking shape — a youngster whose fearless cricket is making people sit up and watch.
Article Summary: Former India opener Kris Srikkanth believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the potential to become one of the biggest names in world cricket. The 15-year-old has continued his rapid rise by making a mark in the Duleep Trophy after already setting the IPL and international stages alight. The BCCI is now taking a cautious, long-term approach to his development.

Article Title: ‘This is a mistake’: Srikkanth slams India’s ‘fear-driven’ squad for Afghanistan series

NEW DELHI: India’s decision to field a full-strength squad for the upcoming Afghanistan T20I series has drawn sharp criticism from former cricketer Kris Srikkanth , who believes the selectors missed a valuable opportunity to expose more youngsters to international cricket.Srikkanth described the selection as a “mistake” and suggested that the recent defeats in Ireland and England had influenced the selectors into playing it safe rather than experimenting with the squad.India suffered a 0-2 T20I series defeat against Ireland before being beaten 0-4 by England in July. With the Afghanistan series offering three matches in familiar home conditions, Srikkanth felt it was the ideal setting to give fringe players a longer run.“After the series losses in Ireland and England, the selectors have decided not to take a chance and picked a full-strength squad for Afghanistan. They are going all guns blazing, but this is a mistake. It's against teams like Afghanistan that you should try out youngsters. Instead, you've picked a full-strength squad out of fear,” Srikkanth said on his YouTube channel.Srikkanth also questioned why the selectors had moved so quickly back towards an experienced combination after using the Zimbabwe series to test players outside the regular setup.“It feels like a desperation move after the Ireland and England losses. But this squad is almost the same as the one they picked for England,” he added.India have named a 15-member squad for the three T20Is, with Shreyas Iyer continuing as captain and Tilak Varma as his deputy. Jasprit Bumrah, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Shivam Dube and Varun Chakaravarthy are among the experienced names included, while 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has retained his place after an encouraging Zimbabwe series.The Afghanistan series will be played in New Delhi on September 13, 15 and 17, with all three games scheduled at the Arun Jaitley Stadium.Bumrah's return is, however, subject to fitness clearance, as are Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana. Hardik Pandya, meanwhile, has missed out after suffering another setback during his rehabilitation.The former India captain also raised concerns over the inclusion of players whose match fitness remains untested.“These four have not proved match-fitness. So on what basis are they subject to fitness? Just because you prove your fitness at the Bengaluru CoE, are you fit? That's how Harshit Rana went to England, and then what happened to him there? So match fitness is important,” said Srikkanth.His comments come as Bumrah, Nitish, Sundar and Rana are all awaiting fitness clearance before their participation in the Afghanistan series is confirmed.For Srikkanth, however, the bigger issue is the opportunity cost. Rather than using the three-match series to assess emerging options, he believes India have responded to their recent setbacks by reverting to a familiar combination.(NOTE: *Subject to fitness clearance)

Article Title: Women’s Asia Cup: ‘Focus on cricket, not the noise,’ Mithali Raj tells India ahead of Pakistan clash
Article Text:
File Pic: Harmanpreet Kaur leads out the team. (Getty Images)

BENGALURU: With a 137-run win over Hong Kong, India sealed their place in the Women’s Asia Cup semifinals with a match to spare. Their final league outing, however, will be their toughest test yet after they brushed aside minnows Thailand and Hong Kong in their opening two games.On Saturday in Dubai, Harmanpreet Kaur and her team take on cross-border rivals Pakistan in what could serve as a dress rehearsal ahead of next week’s semifinal.With India’s middle order still a concern, former India captain Mithali Raj has urged the team to focus on cricket rather than get consumed by the noise surrounding the rivalry.“You prepare for the cricket, not the noise. Understand your role, anticipate what the opposition may do and know how you will respond. We cannot control what people say outside, but we can control our preparation, communication and reaction under pressure. Clarity of role makes it easier to block out the noise,” the former star batter told TOI.India have dominated Pakistan in T20 cricket, winning 17 of their 20 meetings, but Mithali believes the numbers matter little once the two sides walk out.“It’s an emotional and traditional rivalry. The India vs Pakistan game means a lot to each player.Winning this game is a matter of pride and therefore, the added pressure on the team to perform,” she said.Sending a message to the Indian team, the 43-year-old added: “For the players, it is a cricket match after all, and it’s important to keep calm to do well on the ground. If you focus too much on what it means outside the boundary, you create unnecessary pressure. The atmosphere and expectations will be different, but once you cross the boundary, you have to focus on your role and the team’s plans. I believe India, of course, are the favourites to win the match. ”Mithali also believes the Asia Cup should be viewed as more than just preparation for the upcoming Asian Games , where India will defend the gold medal they won on their debut in the previous edition.“Having lost the last edition of the Asia Cup, India will be looking to reclaim the title. I don’t think they will necessarily look at this tournament only as preparation for the Asian Games,” she pointed out.For the developing teams in the competition, Mithali feels the tournament offers an important platform to measure their progress against the best.“The Asia Cup allows developing sides to test themselves against the best. The gap in experience and resources still exists, but it is narrowing. With cricket now an Olympic sport and also part of the Asian Games, teams have more platforms to compete.”“If you look at the recent two World Cups across different formats, teams like Pakistan and Bangladesh have shown that they can put the top teams under pressure. Tournaments like the Asia Cup are also a good indicator of how much the game has developed across different countries,” Mithali explained.(Watch ACC Women's Asia Cup 2026 on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD and Sony LIV)
Article Summary: India beat Hong Kong to reach the semifinals of the Women's Asia Cup. Harmanpreet Kaur's side take on cross-border rivals Pakistan on Saturday. Former India captain Mithali Raj has urged the team to focus on cricket.

Article Title: Lhuan-dre-Pretorius’ 101, Connor Esterhuizen’s 88 help South Africa survive Namibia scare to reach final
Article Text:
Lhuan-dre Pretorius

Pretorius, Esterhuizen power South Africa to 228

Namibia launch stunning fightback

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Africa held their nerve in a thrilling high-scoring contest against Namibia, securing an 11-run victory at the Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoek on Friday to book their place in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series final.After posting a mammoth 228/4 in 20 overs, South Africa were pushed all the way by the hosts, who finished on 217/3 despite a spirited chase. The result means South Africa will face Zimbabwe in the final on Sunday.South Africa's innings was dominated by a spectacular opening partnership between Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Connor Esterhuizen. Esterhuizen smashed 88 off just 40 balls, clearing the ropes eight times and hitting six fours, while Pretorius produced the innings of the day with a magnificent 101 off 53 balls, including five fours and eight sixes. Their opening stand was worth 156 runs and laid the foundation for a daunting total.Pretorius reached his maiden T20I century in the final over, completing the landmark in 52 deliveries. His hundred came only days after he had narrowly missed out against Zimbabwe with a career-best 94.South Africa eventually finished on 228/4, setting Namibia a required run rate of 11.45 an over.Namibia refused to surrender despite the enormous target.Openers Louren Steenkamp and Jan Frylinck gave the hosts exactly the start they needed, keeping pace with the asking rate and putting South Africa under pressure.Frylinck produced a sensational 72 off 36 balls, while Steenkamp contributed a composed 61 off 44, ensuring Namibia remained firmly in the contest for much of the chase. Namibia crossed 200 with the game still alive, leaving South Africa facing a tense finish.The final overs belonged to South Africa's bowlers as they finally managed to squeeze the boundaries out of Namibia.With the hosts needing a huge finish, Nqobani Mokoena delivered the decisive blow in the final over. He dismissed Ruben Trumpelmann caught behind, with Connor Esterhuizen completing the catch, as Namibia ended on 217/3 after 19.6 overs.The result also confirmed the final line-up: South Africa will meet Zimbabwe in Sunday's final, while Namibia's impressive campaign ends with a narrow defeat despite their remarkable 217-run chase.
Article Summary: South Africa beat Namibia by 11 runs in Namibia T20I Tri-Series final. Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Connor Esterhuizen hit centuries for hosts. South Africa will face Zimbabwe in Sunday's final. Namibia's impressive campaign ends with a narrow defeat.

Article Title: Pakistan coach Mike Hesson breaks silence on mid-England series shake-up, says 'I really don’t know what happened'
Article Text:

Hesson clears air on Rizwan, Agha and Imam

Hesson wants more variety in bowling attack

Pakistan’s interim red-ball coach Mike Hesson has distanced himself from the decision to release seven players from the Test squad ahead of the third and final Test against England, saying three senior players had already been sent home before he was asked to take charge.The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) made sweeping changes after the visitors suffered heavy defeats in the first two Tests. England won the series opener by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley before securing a 194-run victory at Lord’s to take an unassailable 2-0 lead.Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Imam-ul-Haq, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad were released from the squad, while head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also relieved of their duties. Hesson was subsequently handed charge of the Test side for the Edgbaston clash, starting September 9.Speaking to the media in Birmingham on Friday, Hesson said he had no role in the decision to release Rizwan, Agha and Imam, insisting that the trio had already left the squad when he was approached to manage the Test team.“When they (Pakistan Cricket Board) told me if I could manage the side for the final Test, these three players (Rizwan, Agha and Imam) were already released from the squad and (were) on their way home.So, I really don't know what happened there,” Hesson said.While making it clear that he was not involved in the decision concerning the three senior players, Hesson acknowledged that he did have a role in reshaping the rest of the squad.“I was involved in the release of the rest of the players and the inclusion of some new players,” he said.Hesson explained that he had recently returned from Japan after his involvement with Pakistan’s white-ball setup when the PCB asked him to take over the red-ball side.“We already had a white-ball camp in Lahore and I had just returned from Japan where the Asian Games are taking place, when I was asked if I could manage the red-ball squad,” he added.With Pakistan already out of contention for the Test series, Hesson said his priority was to create a more balanced squad for the final match.“I decided to make some changes in the squad to get balance into the squad and my emphasis has been on having a bowling attack which has variety and where we have a couple of bowling all-rounders,” he said.The revamped squad includes Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, along with uncapped players Arafat Minhas, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Saad Baig, Mohammad Imran and Razaullah.
Article Summary: Mike Hesson says he had no role in decision to release Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha and Imam-ul-Haq. Three senior players had already been sent home when Hesson was asked to take charge of the Test side. Hesson said his priority was to create a more balanced squad for the final Test.

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest. The state government also presented her with a cheque of Rs 10 lakh as part of the felicitation.Speaking at the event, Saha highlighted Dey’s difficult journey from a small village in South Tripura to the top of the Commonwealth Games podium.
